raw_report.note: Raw local report includes every reference element; this published summary omits large vectors.

blas_provider.method: Separate ctypes process loaded the same library under the same environment after measurement; no model imported.

post_measurement_changes.description: After this fresh-export run, the controller gained strict requested-fixture case/configuration validation, records additional inherited optimization/GC controls, and also requests one thread via BLIS_NUM_THREADS/GOTO_NUM_THREADS. Model, kernels, inputs, outputs, measurement loops and tolerances did not change. No rerun was needed for these fixture-validation/provenance changes.

measurement_notes: CPU float64, dropout 0, deterministic original PyTorch model weights exported before timing; no checkpoint download.
Full inference includes all B*T logits plus cross-entropy; last-token inference follows upstream targets=None and returns B*1*V logits.
Inference timings are five per-process samples after one warmup; values shown in the summary are medians. Cases use fresh processes; timings are advisory on a shared host.
Build wall time, process wall time and model/input load time are separate. Process wall time includes vector formatting/output and is not kernel throughput.

Training samples are two consecutive AdamW steps for numerical verification, not a warmed throughput benchmark. Native AdamW moments are allocated before the timer; PyTorch initializes moments lazily inside the first timed optimizer step. Use later optimizer steps when comparing optimizer work.
PyTorch forward/backward timings use upstream autograd; native training includes explicit analytic gradients, including allocating the gradient arrays.
all_ignored_loss_is_nan is checked explicitly as a Boolean; every all-ignored gradient is compared to zero. Ordinary numerical results must be finite.
The native BLAS executions load the standalone shared library; they do not import NumPy, SciPy or PyTorch. The exporter/oracle uses CPython and PyTorch.
